title: Celebrating One Year with the Batch 65 Fusion Festival Programming Contest
excerpt: Celebrating one year of Batch 65 with problem-solving excitement and camaraderie at our first intra-batch contest.
author: Fazley Rabbi
cover_alt: Participants coding in the computer lab during the Batch 65 Fusion Festival Programming Contest.
body:
## One Year of Brotherhood, Learning, and Code

Completing our **first year** at **Southeast University (SEU)** as part of **CSE Batch 65** was a milestone worth celebrating. Over the past twelve months, we navigated introductory coursework, spent countless evenings debugging syntax errors, and gradually built a shared love for algorithms and problem-solving. To commemorate this special anniversary, we organized the **1st Intra Batch 65 Fusion Festival Programming Contest** in **December 2024**.

## The Contest Arena: Energy, Logic, and Balloons

The university computer lab transformed into a buzzing arena of focus and friendly rivalry. Monitors glowed with code editors, keyboards clicked in rapid unison, and balloons were delivered to workstations to celebrate each accepted solution. The contest featured a thoughtfully crafted set of algorithmic challenges designed to push our logical thinking while encouraging newcomers to experience competitive programming firsthand. Watching the live scoreboard shift turn-by-turn brought both tension and great cheer.

## Mentorship and Community Spirit

Beyond the competition, the event reflected the growing strength of our community. Senior mentors and faculty members stood by to encourage participants, review problem approaches, and share insights on competitive programming strategies. Events like the Fusion Festival remind us that growth in computer science is not an isolated endeavor—it thrives when classmates learn, compete, and celebrate milestones together.

These photographs capture the contest atmosphere, scoreboard presentations, and moments with our teammates and friends from Batch 65.
